page.text:
The characterization of set equality by mutual inclusion—often called the
*double containment* principle—is one of the most powerful and heavily
employed proof strategies in all of mathematics. To demonstrate that two
independently defined sets $A$ and $B$ are identical, one routinely
proves the two directions $A \subseteq B$ and $B \subseteq A$ as separate
lemmas.
